scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Peg mechanics: if a stablecoin trades at $0.98 and can be redeemed for $1.00, arbitrageurs buy and redeem it, pushing the price back up. The peg is only as strong as redemption access and reserve quality. History (research these as case studies): Fiat-backed, Cash/treasuries held by an issuer, Issuer, bank and custodian risk; freezes; redemption limited to approved parties. Crypto-backed, Over-collateralised on-chain crypto, Collateral crash, liquidations, oracle failure. Synthetic or hedged, Derivative positions (for example spot + short perp), Funding turns negative, exchange/venue risk, model risk. Algorithmic, Mostly its own mechanism or sister token, Reflexive death spiral when confidence breaks.

scenes.title: Worked example: A fiat-backed coin trades at $0.97
steps: A minter makes ~2.9% per coin by buying and redeeming, so arbitrage should…
You can't redeem, so you rely on minters acting and on the reserves being…
If markets doubt the reserves, minters may not step in, and the discount can…
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. A fiat-backed coin trades at $0.97. Redemption is $1.00 minus a 0.1% fee, but only for verified institutional minters. A minter makes about 2.9% per coin by buying and redeeming, so arbitrage should restore the peg. You can't redeem, so you rely on minters acting and on the reserves being real. If markets doubt the reserves, minters may not step in, and the discount can grow.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: I know the type and backing of every stablecoin I hold
I know who can redeem, and how
I don't treat "different stablecoins" as diversified if they share issuers or collateral
I have a depeg exit rule (e.g. sell or rotate below $0.99 for longer than X hours)
scenes.vo: Here's your checklist. Do it now, for real. First, I know the type and backing of every stablecoin I hold. Next, I know who can redeem, and how. Then, I don't treat "different stablecoins" as diversified if they share issuers or collateral. And finally, I have a depeg exit rule (for example sell or rotate below $0.99 for longer than X hours).

scenes.q: What keeps a fiat-backed stablecoin near $1?
scenes.a: Redemption for $1 of reserves, plus arbitrageurs who can redeem.

scenes.a: No. They share the same failure point.
